open.speaker: ms_dot
lines: Local studies is by request. Coats on the rack, not the chairs. Voices down; this is a library, not the Register.
You'll want 1966. Everybody wants 1966. I'll tell you now the fiche is scratched where everybody stops the reel.
She's catalogued the scratches. I'd put money on it.

passives.line: The nameplate says Rainey. You know a Dot Rainey. She's two hundred miles away behind a different counter.
The return cart has a slip for a 1911 plat book and no book. Somebody asked for it this week and she hasn't stopped thinking about it.

options.text: Not 1966. December 1967. The week after the bridge.

fail.line: The bridge is the 15th. Everybody knows the 15th. Sit down and wind the reel like the rest of them.

options.text: Where do people stop the reel?

voices.speaker: ms_dot
lines: See that you do. The last pair didn't. Grey suits, Tuesday, talking across the reader like it was a lunch counter.
I shushed them. The tall one apologised like he'd been shushed before. By me.
By her. Not in this building, I'd guess.

dec67.speaker: ms_dot
lines: ...The 18th. Nobody asks for the 18th. They ask for the 15th, and they cry, and I bring the tissues.
The 18th has a two-inch notice on page six. You'll want page six. I'll have the reel on.
Page six is where you bury a thing you had to print.

scratches.speaker: ms_dot
lines: Front page, November 16th, 1966. Worn white at the headline and clean underneath. Nobody reads past the picture.
And one more place. December '67, deep in. One person stopped there, over and over, until I asked her to stop.

hub.speaker: ms_dot
lines: Request what you're requesting. I've a cart to shelve.

static.line: Her hand keeps going to the desk drawer. Not the card file. The drawer. Ask her what's in it before she locks it.

options.text: There's a slip for the 1911 plat book on the cart and no book.
Do you know a Dot Rainey in Sutton?
She wrote 'not hoax'. You knew her.
(Wind the reel back without being asked.)

plat.speaker: ms_dot
lines: The suit requested it. I told him it was out. He asked since when, and I told him, and he wrote it down and thanked me by name.
Then he asked for the card. Her card. I said library cards are not public record. He said, 'They are where I work.'
He didn't get it. It's in my desk, not the file. Has been since 1968.
A card out of the file for twenty-six years. That's not procedure. That's a vigil.

plat_fail.speaker: ms_dot
lines: A slip is a slip. Things get requested. Shelve your own curiosity.
The plat's in the county clerk's too, if you want to bother him instead.

rainey.speaker: ms_dot
lines: ...There's a Rainey in every county in this state. Common as fence posts.
She wrote me once. 1968. Asked had a woman named Weller been in. I wrote back that the card was still open and I'd not cancel it.
She never wrote again. Neither did I. That's how Raineys are.
Two women keeping one card open for twenty-six years, and neither one will say why.

rainey_fail.speaker: ms_dot
lines: I know a great many people, and I don't discuss them with strangers across my own desk.
You'll find the fiche where it was. Wind it back when you're done.

gus_card.speaker: ms_dot
lines: (She reads it with her glasses off, close to her face.) Not hoax. That's her hand. She wrote a complaint about our heating in that hand.
She sat at that reader three days. She found what she wanted on the second and stayed the third anyway. I never knew why.
She was waiting for someone to come in and tell her she was wrong.

rewind.speaker: ms_dot
lines: You can keep the reader till closing. The 1967 reel's already on it. Somebody put it there and I haven't taken it off.
